O. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard
( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 August 1979, after the draft finalized by the Umbrellas Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Devision Council. 0.2 This standard was first pubjished in 1964. Since then many suggesThis standard is being revised tions were received for its improvement. to take care of the suggestions received from time to time. 0.3 Umbrellas are being manufactured in the country in large quantity both for domestic consumption and export. By `and large, the manufacturers of umbrellas procure the various parts from different component manufacturers. It is, therefore, necessary that Indian Standards should be made available for the complete umbrella as well as for the components. 0.4 Umbrellas are assemble.d with either steel tubes fitted with handles or cane or bamboo sticks suitably bent at one end into a handle. While umbrellas with tubes allow interchangeability of components, the cane and bamboo sticks, which vary in diameters from piece to piece, do not The fittings, therefore, will have to be allow any interchangeability. manufactured in many sizes. 0.5 Tubes are usually fitted with two stoppers for the two positions of the runner in the assembled umbrellas. In the case of flexus ribs, however, the stopper at the handle end is not required. When ordering tubes alone, this point may be borne in mind by the purchasers. 0.6 The shapes of the handles have not been specified as these are usually according to the dictates of fashion. 0.7 This standard contains clauses which call for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier and which permit the purchaser to use his The relevant clauses are option for selection to suit his requirements. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8. 3

IS t 2918-1979

5. WORKMANSHIP

AND FINISH

5.1 Workmanship 5.1.1 Handle the tube. `X'he the tube. The the tube meant to hold the ball
shall be provided with a suitable reinforcement for fixing reinforcement shall have a central hole to accommodate diameter and the depth of the hole shall be suitable for for it. The handle shall be provided with a suitable cup ends of the ribs when the umbrella is in closed position.

5.1.2 The tubes shall be round and straight to have smooth movement of runner while opening and closing the umbrella. The stoppers shall be properly fitted to the tube and when depressed and released ten times with Shape of the stoppers the thumb these will return to normal position. shall be such as to have a smooth opening of umbrella. Upper stopper shall be such as not to allow the runner to slip back of its own unce the The stoppers shall not have sharp edges and shall umbrella is opened. not be so hard as to hurt the thumb. cleaned and 5.2 Finish -- The tubes end stoppers shall be thoroughly freed from rust and scale and shall be suitably protected against corrosion. to It pzzinted, they shall be stove tmamelled with paint conforming 6
